title: Deployment Storyboard and Risk Reduction Calculator
author: Lena Kim
content:
Overview

This page is a single-stop enablement artifact for technical and commercial reps to: (1) frame deployment scenarios for prospects, (2) quantify near-term risk reduction and unit economics gains from using Redwood Inference, and (3) run a bounded pilot with deterministic success criteria. Use the storyboard during pre-sales discovery and the risk-reduction calculator during solution design and pricing conversations.

Target audience

- Platform engineers and ML engineers evaluating model-serving options.
- Infra/Cloud Architects evaluating cost and capacity trade-offs.
- Security/compliance leads validating data controls and auditability.
- Sales engineers and AE preparing pilot/POC statements of work.

Key outcomes for a pilot (recommended 4–6 weeks)

1. Validate 99th-percentile latency SLOs for primary LLM route.
2. Demonstrate >= 30% per-token cost improvement vs baseline inference path (measured tokens-incremental cost).
3. Collect production prompt set regressions and ensure no quality regressions beyond agreed thresholds.
4. Confirm routing / fallback behavior across region and model variants.

Solution framing checklist (for discovery)

- Primary workload: chat, generation, embeddings, reranking.
- Expected traffic: RPS, average prompt length, distribution of max_tokens.
- Latency targets: p50, p95, p99 (ms).
- Availability/SLA requirements and allowed maintenance windows.
- Data residency and encryption requirements (KMS/HSM).
- Integration constraints (VPC peering, private link, on-prem connector).
- Success metrics for pilot (throughput, cost per 1k tokens, regression rate).

Competitive positioning (short brief)

This section provides concise messaging for common competitors during technical conversations. Use the competitor-by-issue format below.

1) Managed LLM API providers (examples: large public LLM vendors)
- Primary competitor claims: simple API, larger model catalog, managed scaling.
- Redwood counter: production-first runtime with deterministic latency and cost controls, transparent per-route telemetry, and rollouts designed for safe, non-disruptive upgrades. We surface token-level cost breakdowns and offer Dedicated/Private deployment modes for predictable capacity and isolation.

2) Self-hosted inference runtimes (examples: open-source serving stacks)
- Primary competitor claims: full control, no vendor lock-in, lower long-run costs.
- Redwood counter: we combine a GPU-optimized runtime (kernel selection, KV cache, continuous batching) with orchestration, auto-fallbacks, model variant cataloging, and enterprise-grade ops (SLA-backed Dedicated, Private VPC). For teams that want control without building orchestration and observability, Redwood reduces time-to-production and operational risk.

3) Cloud-managed GPU endpoints and model platforms
- Primary competitor claims: integrated with cloud provider, proximity to data.
- Redwood counter: cross-cloud and hybrid routing policies, quantization and batching recommendations tuned by model and sequence distribution, and cost-aware routing to reduce unit economics. Our Private offering supports air-gapped/on-prem packaging when regulator demands it.

Pitch outline (technical deck recommended slides)

- Slide 1: Title + 1-line value prop (latency, cost, reliability across deployments).
- Slide 2: Customer pain snapshot (specific workload metrics).
- Slide 3: Redwood architecture at a glance (serving runtime, smart router, cache, deployment modes).
- Slide 4: Pilot plan + success criteria (SLOs + economics).
- Slide 5: Demo & benchmark highlights (p50/p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens).
- Slide 6: Security & compliance controls (KMS, audit logs, private control plane).
- Slide 7: Pricing options and proposed pilot commercial terms.
- Slide 8: Next steps and rollout timeline.

Pilot commercial templates and pricing guidance

Base assumptions used in the risk calculator:
- Baseline inference cost: $0.35 per 1k tokens served (customer self-hosted or cloud-managed baseline).
- Redwood hosted API estimate: $0.50 per 1k tokens (includes managed model catalog and streaming).
- Redwood Dedicated estimate: 0.28–0.40 per 1k tokens depending on commitment level and batching profile.
- Pilot duration: 4 weeks (proof-of-concept) or 8–12 weeks (integration + load testing).

Suggested pilot commercial templates (pick one):
- Lightweight trial (4 weeks): free limited credits + Redwood engineering time for infra setup (up to 8 engineer-hours). Success commitment: reproduce 1 representative workload and collect metrics.
- Standard pilot (6–8 weeks): fixed professional services block (40 engineer-hours) + discounted Dedicated capacity at 50% list for pilot period. Success commitment: meet p99 latency target and >= 15% cost improvement vs baseline.
- Enterprise pilot (8–12 weeks): scope includes private deployment options, compliance evidence package, and runbook handover. Commercial: SOW + 90-day evaluation license.

Risk Reduction Calculator (how to use)

Step-by-step:
1. Collect inputs from the discovery checklist: RPS, avg prompt length, baseline cost per 1k tokens, desired latency SLO.
2. Estimate batching and cache hit rate: typical prefix cache for few-shot prompts is 10–30% depending on pattern; set a conservative 15% for initial calc.
3. Choose deployment mode: Hosted (fastest), Dedicated (predictable cost), Private (compliance). Each has a modeled per-token cost range.
4. Run the sensitivity table (copy this section into your spreadsheet):

| Input | Example value | Notes |
|------|---------------:|------|
| RPS | 20 | requests per second |
| Avg tokens per request | 250 | includes prompt + completion |
| Baseline cost (per 1k tokens) | $0.35 | customer-reported |
| Estimated cache hit rate | 15% | prefix/KV cache reduces token generation |
| Target p99 latency | 350 ms | application requirement |

Example calculator outputs (rounded):
- Raw tokens served per day = RPS * 86400 * avg tokens = 20 * 86400 * 250 = 432M tokens/day.
- Effective tokens after 15% cache = 367.2M tokens/day.
- Baseline daily cost = 367.2M / 1000 * $0.35 = $128,520/day.
- Redwood Dedicated lower-bound daily cost (0.28/1k) = 367.2M / 1000 * $0.28 = $102,816/day.
- Estimated daily savings = $25,704/day (~20% cost savings).

Guidance notes:
- Quantization and kernel selection can further reduce serving cost on Dedicated (we commonly see an additional 10–25% improvement for compatible models).
- Batching policies tuned to request size distribution are the largest driver of cost variance.

Security & Compliance FAQ (talking points for SEs)

Q: Where does customer data persist and who can access it?
A: For Hosted: transient KV caches and logs are encrypted at rest; customer data is logically separated and access-controlled. For Dedicated and Private: customer-managed VPC and optional on-prem package ensure data never leaves defined boundaries. Role-based access with audit logs is enabled for all modes.

Q: How do we support KMS/HSM integrations?
A: We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and vendor HSMs via a customer-provided key provisioning workflow. For Private deployments, HSM can be local.

Q: What evidence do you provide for audits?
A: We supply configuration export, audit log extracts, architecture diagrams, and an attestation checklist. For enterprise pilots we include a compliance evidence bundle (SOC/ISO references where applicable).

Q: How are model and prompt leakage risks mitigated?
A: We support per-route token redaction, prompt filtering, deterministic caching policies, and model variant pinning to avoid unexpected model pulls. Canary rollouts and automated regression evals reduce ML drift risk.

Case study snapshot (anonymized)

Customer: Large SaaS company (B2B productivity)
Problem: Unpredictable latency and 3x higher per-token cost on their in-house GPU endpoints during peak.
Pilot scope: 6-week Dedicated evaluation for text generation routes and embeddings.
Outcome: Achieved p95 latency reduction of 45% and 38% per-token cost improvement after batching and prefix cache tuning. Production rollout plan included staggered canaries and fallbacks.

Playbook: Pilot runbook (high level)

1) Pre-engagement (owner: AE/SE)
- Collect discovery checklist and signed pilot MSA.
- Confirm lead SE and customer contacts.
- Provision initial capacity (Hosted or Dedicated trial).

2) Week 0–1: Onboarding (owner: SE + Solutions Eng)
- Validate network connectivity (VPC peering, Private Link).
- Upload representative prompt set and baseline traffic replay.
- Configure metrics collection and SLO dashboards (p50/p95/p99, error rates, cost breakdown).

3) Week 2–4: Performance tuning (owner: Runtime Eng + SE)
- Tune batching, KV cache and quantization profile.
- Run load tests to p95 and p99 targets.
- Evaluate model variants and fallback policies.

4) Week 4–6: Validation and handover (owner: Customer + SE)
- Confirm success criteria met.
- Deliver runbooks, traffic routing plan, and rollback steps.
- Propose next-phase contract (Dedicated commit or Private deployment SOW).

Ownership and escalation

- AE: commercial owner, SOW sign-off.
- SE: pilot technical owner, runbook execution.
- Runtime engineering (on-call): support for kernel/serving issues during load tests.
- Customer success: onboarding and handover for production.

Suggested next steps for an AE or SE

1. Use the discovery checklist in this doc during the next technical call.
2. Populate the calculator with customer baseline numbers and propose a pilot template.
3. If customer has strict compliance needs, flag early for Private deployment stream and involve security team.
